name: MH-Z19C NDIR CO2 sensor
description: Winsen infrared (NDIR) CO2 sensor, 400-5000 ppm (2000 and 10000 ppm ranges exist), 1 ppm resolution, accuracy ±(50 ppm + 5 % of reading), temperature compensated. UART at 9600 baud with 3.3 V logic (5 V compatible) plus a PWM output and an HD zero-calibration input; needs a 5 V supply (4.5-5.5 V) that can deliver 150 mA. Sold as: Winsen MH-Z19C terminal version with 7-pin JST cable (pin 1-7: HD, reserved, GND, Vin, RXD, TXD, PWM), the same sensor also comes as a pin version with two side headers.
eli5: Measures how much carbon dioxide is in the air, so you know when a room needs fresh air.

pins.name: HD
pins.description: Pin 1, manual zero-point calibration input: holding it low for over 7 s sets the current reading to 400 ppm. Leave unconnected for normal use

pins.name: Vin
pins.description: Pin 4, supply 5 V (4.5-5.5 V), at least 150 mA; do not use 3.3 V

pins.name: RXD
pins.description: Pin 5, UART data into the sensor (3.3 V TTL): wire to the microcontroller's TX

pins.name: TXD
pins.description: Pin 6, UART data out of the sensor (3.3 V TTL): wire to the microcontroller's RX

pins.name: PWM
pins.description: Pin 7, PWM output (1004 ms cycle, Cppm = range x (TH - 2 ms) / (T - 4 ms)); not needed when using UART

supplierQuery: MH-Z19C CO2 sensor NDIR UART terminal cable
buildNotes: Power Vin from 5 V (ESP32 VIN/5V, Pico VBUS); on 3.3 V the reading goes low or the sensor stops. The supply must deliver 150 mA (125 mA peaks).
Cross the serial lines: microcontroller TX to sensor RXD, microcontroller RX to sensor TXD. 9600 baud, 8N1, 3.3 V logic.
Read CO2 by sending FF 01 86 00 00 00 00 00 79; the reply is FF 86 HIGH LOW x x x x checksum, CO2 = HIGH*256 + LOW ppm.
Check the checksum: (0xFF - (byte1+...+byte7)) + 1. A mismatch usually means a loose wire or the wrong baud rate.
Allow 1 minute of preheat (longer for stable readings). Leave the reserved pin unconnected; HD and PWM are optional.

example.code:
from machine import UART, Pin
import time
from mhz19c import MHZ19C

u = UART({UART_ID}, baudrate=9600, tx=Pin({RXD}), rx=Pin({TXD}))
sensor = MHZ19C(u)
while True:
    try:
        print('CO2=%d ppm' % sensor.read_co2())
    except OSError as e:
        print(e)
    time.sleep(1)
